tagline: Seven miles of Post Road between the moraine and the ponds.
intro: Seven miles of the Post Road cross Charlestown between the South Kingstown and Westerly lines, divided all the way, with a median very wide over half its length whose plantings hide the oncoming traffic in many places. On the north the wooded edge of the glacial moraine rides along beside the road. On the south the land flattens into outwash plain, and the lower growth gives glimpses of the salt ponds.

The town's 2004 stewardship plan called the road the southern boundary of the Narragansett settlement lands, and counted the 1667 General Stanton Inn and the 1730 Wilcox Tavern among the historic sites signed from it.

moments.title: Charlestown Moraine
moments.text: The rise edging much of the north side is soil and rock the last ice sheets dropped at their southernmost reach, grown up in oak, maple, white pine and red cedar.

moments.title: Fort Ninigret
moments.text: Its 1883 dedication called it the oldest military post on the Atlantic coast, a fort most historians credit to the Dutch West India Company or Portuguese explorers before 1637, beside a Niantic settlement.

moments.title: Burlingame State Park
moments.text: Rhode Island's largest campground opened on Watchaug Pond in 1934 and served through the 1930s as the state's main base for the Civilian Conservation Corps.

sources.label: Charlestown Conservation Commission, Route 1 Scenic Roadway Stewardship Plan (2004)
